title: Alpha-5 encode/decode vectors from the Space-Track table, with boundaries and invalid inputs

checks.description: An Alpha-5 catalog field decodes as (letter value)*10000 + digits with A=10 ... Z=33 and I, O unused; 'I', 'O' and lowercase are invalid.
Integers 100000-339999 encode to the Alpha-5 table; below 100000 encode as five digits with leading zeros; above 339999 cannot be encoded.
NORAD_CAT_ID parses as an integer in every OMM format, including values of six and nine digits; leading zeros and an explicit '+' are legal in KVN.
TLE epoch years 57-99 map to 1957-1999 and 00-56 to 2000-2056; the resulting ISO epoch equals the OMM EPOCH string.

parse_epoch accepts every CCSDS 502.0-B-3 7.5.10 epoch form in vectors/ccsds-epoch-strings.json (calendar and day-of-year, with or without a fraction and a Z, second 60) and returns the instant each denotes (within 2 us; a leap second may read as 23:59:59 or as the next midnight), and rejects the five invalid forms.

provides: all 24 letters and both skips, the six official examples, range boundaries, invalid letters and lowercase
gaps: vectors are not element sets; they test the mapping only

sources: https://www.space-track.org/documentation (FAQ 'What is Alpha-5?' and TLE page 'Alpha 5' section; read 2026-09-20)
CelesTrak GP formats FAQ (CelesTrak itself does not emit Alpha-5): https://celestrak.org/NORAD/documentation/gp-data-formats.php
vectors/alpha5.json.rule: Objects 100000-339999: first character is a letter with value 10-33 (A=10, B=11, ... skipping I and O ... Z=33) followed by the last four digits. Objects below 100000: five digits, leading zeros retained. Alpha-5 appears only in TLE/3LE columns 3-7 of lines 1 and 2; OMM NORAD_CAT_ID is always an integer.

decode_invalid.reason: lowercase is not defined by Space-Track; a lenient decoder that accepts it disagrees with a strict one
only the first character may be a letter
letter only in the first position

encode_unrepresentable.reason: nine-digit ids cannot be encoded; OMM formats required

vectors/alpha5.json.checksum_note: In a TLE checksum the Alpha-5 letter counts 0 (letters, blanks, periods and plus signs count 0; minus signs count 1), per Space-Track and CelesTrak.

sources: CCSDS 502.0-B-3 Table 4-3: NORAD_CAT_ID 'an integer of up to nine digits'
CCSDS 502.0-B-3 7.5.4: integers may have a leading sign and leading zeroes
SANA ndmxml-4.0.0-omm-3.0.xsd and ndmxml-2.0.0-omm-2.0.xsd: NORAD_CAT_ID is xsd:integer
https://www.space-track.org/documentation (FAQ 'What is Alpha-5?' and TLE page 'Alpha 5' section; read 2026-09-20)

valid.note: explicit plus allowed in KVN integers (7.5.4)

invalid_in_omm.reason: Alpha-5 is a TLE-only encoding; OMM NORAD_CAT_ID is an integer
ten digits exceed 'up to nine digits'; schema xsd:integer would accept it, the standard's text does not
empty; keyword is Optional and should be omitted instead

sources: T.S. Kelso, 'Frequently Asked Questions: Two-Line Element Set Format', Satellite Times, January 1998: 'Two-digit years from 57-99 correspond to 1957-1999 and those from 00-56 correspond to 2000-2056.' https://celestrak.org/columns/v04n03/
python-sgp4 io.py implements the same pivot (year < 57 -> +2000)
vectors/two-digit-epoch-year.json.resolution_note: 1e-8 day = 0.000864 s; an 8-decimal day fraction always converts to an exact whole number of microseconds.
vectors/two-digit-epoch-year.json.international_designator_note: The TLE international designator also carries a two-digit launch year (columns 10-11); no document defines its century mapping. This corpus applies the same 57 pivot (see ambiguity object-id-launch-year-pivot).

sources: CCSDS 502.0-B-3 7.5.10: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss[.d->d][Z] or YYYY-DDDThh:mm:ss[.d->d][Z]; all fields with leading zeros; Z optional
iso: the instant each valid string denotes, as 'YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss.ffffff' UTC; a parse_epoch hook is compared with it within 2 us (D-119)

valid.note: CCSDS annex G example, day-of-year form
leap second: ss = 60 permitted (7.5.10 NOTE); a datetime cannot carry second 60, so the instant one second earlier (iso) or the next midnight (iso_alternatives) is accepted

invalid.reason: TLE epoch field, not an OMM epoch
only 'Z' is permitted as time-code terminator in 7.5.10 (the XSD pattern is more permissive)

vectors/ccsds-epoch-strings.json.parser_hazard: A parser hard-coded to '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f' (for example python-sgp4's sgp4.omm.initialize) rejects five of the valid strings above.
